name: Govannon

attributes.attribute: parallel deity to the Irish smith god Goibniu
cleaned the plows at the end of planting
renamed Goban Saor and made builder of early churches

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Govannon was the Welsh god of the forge. He stood as a close match to the Irish smith deity Goibniu, and both served as great craftsmen. The magician king Math worked alongside him. When smelting metal was still new, people saw smithcraft as near magic. Govannon also cleaned the plows after planting so the tools would serve one more season. In the Mabinogion he struck down Dylan, the magical son of Arianrhod, by accident, and the waves of the sea mourned the boy. Later folklore renamed him Goban Saor and made him the builder of early churches. He ruled the elements and weather, so some read him as an old thunder god like Taranis.

okr.objective: Present Govannon as the Welsh smith god, his smithcraft, and his loss of Dylan.
key_results: Govannon is the Welsh forge god, a match to the Irish Goibniu.
He cleaned the plows after planting so they would serve another year.
In the Mabinogion he accidentally killed Arianrhod's son Dylan.
Later folklore cast him as Goban Saor, builder of early churches.
